Done. Auth.js v5 (`next-auth@5.0.0-beta.32`), wired into `src/lib/users.ts` as the user store.

**Why Auth.js over better-auth:** you asked me to wire it into the existing `users.ts`. Auth.js's Credentials provider lets that array stay the source of truth; better-auth would want to own its own tables via a DB adapter, so I'd have been fighting it. JWT sessions mean no database — matching a repo that has none.

**Files**
- `src/lib/users.ts` — kept `listUsers`/`getUser`; added `createUser`, `verifyCredentials`, `upsertOAuthUser`, `getUserByEmail`. `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session (that TODO is gone).
- `src/auth.config.ts` / `src/auth.ts` — split so the Edge-runtime proxy never pulls in bcrypt or the user store.
- `src/proxy.ts` — Next 16 renamed `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`; I used the new convention.
- `src/app/signin`, `src/app/signup`, `src/components/auth-form.tsx`, `src/lib/auth-actions.ts`, `src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts`.

**Verified against a running production build,** not just a compile: wrong password rejected / correct password issues a session; signup → auto sign-in → dashboard; duplicate email caught case-insensitively; sign-out re-locks the page. Google's redirect builds correctly (real PKCE challenge, right `redirect_uri` and scopes) — the actual round trip needs real credentials, which is the one thing placeholders can't cover.

**Three judgment calls worth your attention:**

1. **`/dashboard` is gated twice.** The Next 16 docs say proxy code "should not attempt relying on shared modules" — and CVE-2025-29927 was exactly a middleware-bypass. So proxy only does the optimistic redirect; the real check is `getCurrentUser()` in the page. I tested the bypass header: still redirects, no data leaks.

2. **`AUTH_URL` is uncommented in `.env.example` on purpose.** Auth.js throws `UntrustedHost` and 500s on any production build off Vercel without it — `next dev` hides this completely. I hit it during testing. I set `AUTH_URL` rather than `AUTH_TRUST_HOST=true` because the latter blanket-trusts the `Host` header.

3. **`.gitignore` had a blanket `.env*`** that would have silently swallowed `.env.example`. Added `!.env.example`.

**One thing you should know:** users live in an in-memory array, so **every signup is lost on restart and won't be shared across serverless instances.** That's inherent to the existing `users.ts`, and you scoped this to auth — so I didn't add a database. But this isn't deployable as-is; swapping the array for a real store is the next step, and the function boundaries in `users.ts` are where you'd do it without touching any auth code.

Seeded users `ada@example.com` / `grace@example.com` both use `password123` (documented in `.env.example`). I left a gitignored `.env.local` with a working secret so `npm run dev` runs immediately.
